channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Power
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Citrix confirms NetScaler zero-days exploited worldwide; both flaws are in CISA KEV with a 30 September deadline
item.description: Citrix confirmed on 27 September that two critical flaws in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 (both CVSS 9.5), were exploited in the wild before patches existed. CISA added both to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog with a 30 September federal deadline. CVE-2026-88771 lets an unauthenticated attacker run commands on default configurations; CVE-2026-88772 is a memory flaw reachable when DTLS is enabled, the default on VPN virtual servers. Citrix says multiple customers worldwide were hit but names no sector, and no power-sector compromise has been reported. NetScaler is a common remote-access front door for utility corporate networks, contractors and integrators, so a compromised appliance could become the first hop toward EMS, SCADA and substation networks. CISA advises checking for compromise before patching. - Citrix security bulletin CTX697096 and CISA KEV alert, 27 Sep 2026 (primary); watchTowr Labs 26 Sep; reported by BleepingComputer, SecurityWeek and The Hacker News - watchTowr warning 26 Sep 2026; Citrix confirmation, patches and KEV listing 27 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] Three clusters are exploiting Cisco firewall-manager flaws CVE-2026-20079 and CVE-2026-20316; one shares tooling with Sandworm
item.category: Incident — Exploited firewall management platform, CISA KEV
item.description: Cisco and CISA confirmed on 9 September that CVE-2026-20079, a CVSS 10.0 authentication bypass that lets an unauthenticated attacker run scripts and potentially gain root on Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center, is being exploited; CISA added it to KEV with a 12 September deadline, now passed. Cisco Talos describes three clusters. UAT-12197 deployed a web shell and stole credentials. UAT-11823 used both CVE-2026-20079 and CVE-2026-20316 (CVSS 5.3, low-privilege remote login) to drop reverse shells and then Cyclops Blink malware, with tooling that Talos says overlaps with the Sandworm APT actor — an overlap, not a government attribution. UAT-11988, a ransomware operator, used CVE-2026-20316 and living-off-the-land tools for reconnaissance before deploying Qilin ransomware. Talos reports hotfixes for both flaws and a broader hardening release planned for the week of 16 September; its last update was 21 September and it names no victims or sectors. FMC configures the firewalls that separate corporate networks from generation, substation and DER control. - Cisco Talos analysis, published 9 Sep and updated 21 Sep 2026 (primary); CISA KEV listing 9 Sep 2026 - Exploitation confirmed 9 Sep 2026; Talos update 21 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] Check Point management-server and VPN-gateway flaws were exploited before KEV listing; the federal deadline passed on 25 September
item.category: Incident — Exploited management-server and VPN-gateway flaws, CISA KEV
item.description: CISA added two Check Point flaws to KEV on 22 September. CVE-2026-93616 (CVSS 9.8) is a pre-authentication path traversal in the Security Management web service that allows arbitrary script execution; Check Point saw limited, targeted attacks on 23 July and shipped the fix on 22 September. CVE-2026-85102 (CVSS 9.8) is a pre-authentication remote code execution flaw in Security Gateway and Spark firewalls with VPN certificate handling, patched on 9 September; Check Point reports an exploitation wave beginning 12 September. For a utility these appliances often terminate the VPNs that contractors and integrators use to reach plant and substation networks. The same KEV batch added F5 BIG-IP APM CVE-2026-94127 (CVSS 9.8, OAuth authorization-server configurations, exploited as a zero-day per F5) and an Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw; all four deadlines fell on 25 September. No power-sector victim has been named. - Check Point security advisory, 22 Sep 2026 (primary); CISA KEV alert 22 Sep 2026 - Exploited from 23 Jul 2026 (CVE-2026-93616) and 12 Sep 2026 (CVE-2026-85102); KEV listing 22 Sep, deadline 25 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] CenterPoint Energy confirms customer data was taken; a hacker claims about 7.5 million records and threatens “infrastructure” next
item.category: Incident — Confirmed customer-data breach at a US electric & gas utility
item.description: CenterPoint Energy told the SEC on 15 September that an unauthorized third party obtained personal information relating to a portion of its customers through one of its externally facing systems. Three days earlier a threat actor had posted a 2.5 GB archive on a cybercrime forum, claiming about 7.5 million records and adding: “next time we won’t simply pull data, we’ll start attacking the main infrastructure.” CenterPoint says the incident has not affected the delivery of electric or gas service; it has not confirmed the record count, and no vulnerability, intrusion vector or actor identity has been disclosed. SecurityWeek cautions that hackers often exaggerate and that the data’s validity is unconfirmed, and notes this is not the first CenterPoint data incident. This reads as an IT-side data breach, not an OT compromise — but the actor’s stated intent is a reason for other utilities to check that customer-facing systems are properly segmented from anything that touches control-system networks. - CenterPoint Energy SEC filing, 15 Sep 2026 (primary), reported by SecurityWeek - Data posted for sale 12 Sep 2026; disclosed 15 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] CISA and FBI: a compromised ICS integrator held utilities’ SCADA data — limit what yours can reach
item.category: Threat Intelligence — Joint CISA/FBI guidance drawn from a compromised ICS integrator
item.description: CISA and the FBI released a joint fact sheet on 24 September, “Considerations for Critical Infrastructure Operators Working With Third-Party ICS Integrators.” Its motivating case: in March–April 2025, foreign actors inside a US industrial automation company that does system integration and SCADA programming for customers including power utilities and transportation entities searched for “customers” and “SCADA” and staged nine archives of about 800 files — customer SCADA information, ICS device details and schematics — for exfiltration. The agencies do not name the company, the actor or its country, and do not say any utility was breached. Their advice: write security and supply-chain requirements into integrator contracts, apply least privilege, route remote access through monitored, on-demand channels, know what data integrators hold and where, and be able to operate if an integrator is compromised. - CISA/FBI joint fact sheet (primary), reported by Industrial Cyber and SecurityWeek - Released 24 Sep 2026; cites a March–April 2025 intrusion at the integrator

item.title: [Critical] A predictable session ID lets an attacker bypass authentication on Siemens’ Reyrolle 7SR5 protection relay
item.category: Advisory — Protection relay authentication bypass, no known exploitation
item.description: Siemens published advisory SSA-142885 on 8 September as part of that month’s ICS Patch Tuesday batch. It covers 15 vulnerabilities in the Reyrolle 7SR5 protection relay, with a top CVSS v3.1 score of 9.8: authentication bypass through predictable session identifiers, plus denial of service, privilege escalation and, for someone with physical access, memory corruption and unsigned code execution in maintenance mode. All versions before V2.70 are affected. No in-the-wild exploitation or public exploit code has been reported. Protection relays like this trip breakers to protect equipment during faults; an attacker with unauthenticated access could, in principle, alter settings or block a legitimate trip, though doing so would first require network reach to the relay. - Siemens ProductCERT advisory SSA-142885, 8 Sep 2026 (primary); covered in SecurityWeek’s ICS Patch Tuesday roundup - Published 8 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] Schneider Electric PowerLogic T300 substation RTU has a root privilege-escalation flaw, CVE-2026-77120 (CVSS 8.7)
item.category: Advisory — Substation RTU privilege escalation, no known exploitation
item.description: Schneider Electric’s September ICS Patch Tuesday release on 9 September included a high-severity OS command-injection flaw (CWE-78), CVE-2026-77120, in the PowerLogic T300 — the platform formerly sold as the Easergy T300 RTU — in versions 2.9.8-5620 and earlier. Exploitation needs authenticated SSH access with high privileges, after which an attacker could escalate to root and run administrative functions; the advisory is SEVD-2026-251-02. The same release covered a CVSS 9.2 authentication flaw in Modicon M580 and M580 Safety controllers (CVE-2026-3869), which matters to plant automation at generation sites. Neither is reported as exploited or in KEV. The T300 flaw is a post-access risk rather than a remote entry point, so the priority is controlling who holds SSH credentials on substation RTUs. - Schneider Electric security notice SEVD-2026-251-02 (primary), covered in SecurityWeek’s ICS Patch Tuesday roundup; CVE record via OpenCVE - Published 9 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] One malformed packet can crash TDengine, a database used for industrial and utility telemetry (CVE-2026-42542, CVSS 7.5)
item.category: Advisory — Time-series database used for industrial telemetry, unauthenticated crash
item.description: Ridge Security disclosed CVE-2026-42542, an integer-underflow flaw in the RPC message handler of TDengine, a time-series database used to store industrial, IoT and energy telemetry. A single crafted packet to the default TCP 6030 port can crash the database process without credentials, so an attacker on the network could blind operators to historian and monitoring data. TDengine 3.4.0.0 through 3.4.1.5 is affected and 3.4.1.6 fixes it. Ridge reports no in-the-wild exploitation and no public exploit code, and is withholding its proof of concept. For a generation or transmission operator the exposure depends on whether historians, vendor monitoring products or cloud analytics platforms embed TDengine — a question worth asking vendors, since it is often bundled rather than installed directly. - Ridge Security disclosure (primary), reported by Industrial Cyber (25 Sep) and Dark Reading (28 Sep) - Published 23 Sep 2026

item.title: [Medium] DOE asks the industry how to secure the bulk-power system from foreign-equipment risk; comments are due 9 October
item.category: Policy — DOE request for information on foreign equipment in the bulk-power system
item.description: Executive Order 14421, signed 26 August, declares a national emergency over the security of the US bulk-power system and authorizes the Department of Energy to prohibit, condition or unwind transactions involving foreign-produced bulk-power equipment tied to covered foreign entities. Coverage includes transmission at 69 kV and above, generation needed for reliability, and substation, control-room and generating-station equipment such as transformers, inverters, battery storage and industrial control systems; DOE may also set conditions on previously installed equipment and must issue implementing rules within 120 days. On 9 September DOE published a Federal Register request for information asking utilities, manufacturers, software developers and integrators about equipment definitions, foreign-entity identification, risk criteria, existing-equipment mitigation, remote access and domestic supply. Responses are voluntary and due 9 October 2026. - DOE request for information, Federal Register, 9 Sep 2026 (primary); Executive Order 14421, 26 Aug 2026 - RFI published 9 Sep 2026; comments due 9 Oct 2026; DOE implementing rules due within 120 days of the order

item.title: [Info] FERC approves NERC CIP-014-4; the revised transmission physical-security standard takes effect on 1 October 2028
item.category: Regulation — FERC approves NERC CIP-014-4 (transmission physical security)
item.description: FERC issued an order on 10 September approving NERC Reliability Standard CIP-014-4, published in the Federal Register on 15 September. It consolidates the 30- and 60-month reassessment cycles into a single 36-month cycle, brings jointly owned transmission facilities into scope, requires technically justified thresholds and both steady-state and dynamic simulations, and adds a review of facilities within 1,500 feet of applicable stations. CIP-014-3 retires when the new version takes effect on 1 October 2028; FERC estimates the change affects about 344 transmission owners. The standard is about physical attack, not cyber, but it determines which transmission stations and substations are treated as critical — the same list many owners use to prioritize security work more broadly. - FERC order approving CIP-014-4, Federal Register, 15 Sep 2026 (primary), reported by Industrial Cyber - Order dated 10 Sep 2026; effective 1 Oct 2028
